Synopsis:
    US manufacturing PMI slipped to 54.6 in August from 55.6 in July, missing the 54.6 Reuters consensus of 55.2, but remaining in expansion territory. New orders softened, factory employment dipped, and supply chain stress persisted with supplier deliveries index rising to 59.3. Critically, input price inflation held unchanged at 71.1 — a historically elevated reading — keeping upward pressure on the Fed's inflation mandate. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh flagged more tightening work may be needed. Markets are pricing ~70% odds of a 25bps hike at the Sep 15-16 FOMC meeting. A modest tailwind remains from AI-driven capex and expected inventory restocking.
